title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendor, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This document centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and processes for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the primary reference for employees, managers, and approvers.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and temporary staff across all regions and business units.
- Covers procedural requirements, role responsibilities, approval matrices, and links to operational runbooks and team-specific extensions.

Owner and escalation contacts:
- Policy owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai)
- Primary contact for procurement & expenses: Finance (procurement@redwood.ai)
- Security/Access escalation: Security Team (security@redwood.ai)
- Vendor intake: Legal & Finance (vendor-intake@redwood.ai)

1) Access and permissions
Purpose: Provide consistent rules for granting, reviewing, and revoking access to systems and data.
Key principles:
- Principle of least privilege: grant the minimum set of permissions required to perform the role.
- Role-based access: use predefined roles where available (GitHub, GCP, internal services).
- Time-boxed elevated access: temporary privileges require documented justification and automatic expiry.

Process:
1. Request: employee submits access request via internal Access Portal (link: /tools/access-portal) with justification and owner.
2. Approval: owner or designated approver reviews within 3 business days. Approval matrix: see table below.
3. Provisioning: IT/SRE performs provisioning and logs the change.
4. Verification: requestor verifies access and confirms via portal.
5. Review: quarterly access reviews by team leads; high-sensitivity roles reviewed monthly.
6. Revocation: when employment status changes or role change occurs, managers must revoke within 24 hours for high-risk systems, 72 hours for standard systems.

Approval matrix (summary):
- Low-sensitivity systems (internal docs, Slack): Team lead approval
- Medium-sensitivity (non-PHI customer data, dev infra): Manager + Security reviewer
- High-sensitivity (production databases, KMS, audit logs): Manager + Security + People Ops

Temporary elevated access (jump privileges):
- Request via Access Portal with start and end date (max 7 days, renewals allowed with justification).
- Must include a post-mortem if used for incident response.

2) Change management
Purpose: Ensure predictable, auditable changes to production and shared infrastructure.
Scope: All changes that affect production behavior, capacity, security posture, or customer-facing APIs.

Change categories and process:
- Standard changes (pre-approved routine ops, e.g., certificate renewals): documented in change catalog, no CAB required.
- Normal changes (feature rollouts, infra changes): require change request, risk assessment, test plan, and CAB review.
- Emergency changes (incident remediation): follow emergency change fast-track with retroactive CAB review and post-change RCA.

Change Request checklist (submit in Change Management Portal):
- Change owner and rollback plan
- Impact assessment (services, customers, SLOs)
- Test plan and canary strategy
- Scheduled window and communication plan
- Monitoring and alert thresholds for validation

CAB (Change Advisory Board):
- Weekly scheduled CAB for non-emergency normal changes. Composition: infra leads, SRE, product ops, security representative.
- Approvals must be recorded in the portal with a unique change ID.

Rollback and post-deployment:
- All changes must have a documented rollback plan and quick rollback script where applicable.
- Post-change verification checklist completed within 2 business days; any regressions trigger the rollback process and incident review.

3) Data management
Purpose: Protect data confidentiality, integrity, and availability while enabling product and research work.
Data classification:
- Public: safe to publish externally.
- Internal: company-internal operational data, no PII/PHI.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, business-sensitive information.
- Restricted: regulated data (PHI, regulated finance data), requires specific contractual and technical controls.

Retention and deletion policy (summary table):
| Data type           | Retention default | Owner      | Notes |
|---------------------|-------------------|------------|-------|
| Logs (infra)        | 90 days           | Eng-SRE    | Longer retention via approved request|
| Customer data       | per-contract      | Product    | Follow DPA, deletion on request timelines |
| Employee HR records | 7 years           | People Ops | Comply with local employment law |
| Audit logs (security)| 1 year           | Security   | Immutable store recommended |

Data handling requirements:
- Encryption in transit and at rest for Confidential/Restricted data.
- Access to Confidential/Restricted data requires documented justification and approval from data owner and Security.
- Data export and sharing require legal review for cross-border transfer when outside the customer-approved regions.

Data incident response:
- Report suspected data exposure to security@redwood.ai within 1 hour of detection.
- Security will trigger incident response and notify legal, product, and People Ops as required by the data classification and contracts.

4) Procurement and expenses
Purpose: Standardize purchasing, expense reimbursement, and vendor onboarding.
Principles:
- Purchase approvals must match financial thresholds and budget ownership.
- Use company-approved vendors where available.
- All purchases must have a PO or card transaction linked to an approved budget code.

Approval matrix (high level):
- < $1,000: Requester manager approval
- $1,000 — $25,000: Manager + Finance approval
- > $25,000: Manager + Finance + VP/Director sign-off; legal review if contract involved

Procurement process (step-by-step):
1. Initiate purchase request in Procurement Portal with vendor, estimated cost, budget code, and business justification.
2. Finance reviews within 3 business days and assigns PO if approved.
3. Vendor onboarding (if new): pass vendor questionnaire, risk review by Finance/Legal, and security posture checklist.
4. Purchase execution: Procurement issues PO or assigns corporate card.
5. Receipt and validation: Requester attaches invoice and receipts; Finance matches and closes the PO.

Expenses and travel reimbursement:
- Employees submit expenses in Expense system within 30 days. Attach receipts for amounts > $25.
- Per diem and meal limits: domestic $75/day, international vary by country (refer to travel map).
- Corporate card vs personal reimbursement: prefer corporate card for vendor/airfare; personal cards require manager approval and justification.

5) Vendor management
Lifecycle stages:
1. Vendor identification and selection
2. Risk assessment (security, financial, compliance)
3. Contracting and SLAs (Legal + Finance)
4. Onboarding and technical integration
5. Ongoing performance and periodic review (annual)
6. Offboarding and data return/removal

Vendor risk levels and controls:
- Low risk: SaaS tools with no customer data or PII (annual review).
- Medium risk: tools processing non-sensitive customer data (security questionnaire, SOC2/attestation).
- High risk: services storing or processing customer PII/Restricted data (on-site review, contractual security terms, encryption & audit requirements).

Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Completed vendor questionnaire
- Security/compliance evidence (SOC2, ISO27001) or compensating controls
- Contract with data processing addendum (DPA) if required
- Payment terms and PO set up

6) Travel policies
Booking and approval:
- All business travel must be approved via Travel Portal prior to booking. Approvals follow the expense approval matrix.
- Preferred vendors and travel agencies should be used where available for cost control and duty-of-care.

Safety and duty of care:
- Employees must register international travel with People Ops; emergency contact details required.
- Company emergency assistance vendor contact provided in Travel Portal.

Per diem and allowable expenses:
- Domestic: up to $75/day for meals and incidental expenses.
- International: country-specific per diem (refer to Travel Portal rates).
- Alcohol: reimbursable only when part of a business meal and reasonable.

Travel expense submission:
- Submit within 14 days of travel completion with receipts. Card charges reconciled within 30 days.

7) Internal templates and forms
The following templates are maintained centrally and should be used for all formal requests and records:
- Access request template (Access Portal auto-form)
- Change request template (Change Management Portal)
- Procurement request / PO template (Procurement Portal)
- Vendor questionnaire template (Finance/Legal)
- Travel request & risk acknowledgment (Travel Portal)
- Post-mortem and RCA template (Incident Response)

Governance, training, and audits:
- Annual policy review by People Ops with Security and Finance input.
- Mandatory training: security basics (quarterly), procurement & expense training (annual for managers), data handling training (role-based).
- Periodic audits: access reviews (quarterly), vendor compliance reviews (annual), procurement compliance spot checks.

Definitions and abbreviations:
- PO: Purchase Order
- DPA: Data Processing Agreement
- SOC2: Service Organization Controls Type 2 report
- CAB: Change Advisory Board

Related resources and links:
- Access Portal: /tools/access-portal
- Change Management Portal: /tools/change-portal
- Procurement Portal: /tools/procurement
- Travel Portal: /tools/travel
- Vendor questionnaire: /templates/vendor-questionnaire

Revision history:

Appendix: Quick checklists
- New hire checklist (access, laptop, mandatory training)
- Offboarding checklist (revoke access, return assets, vendor handoff)
- Emergency change checklist (owner, rollback, communication, post-mortem)

If you have questions or need exceptions to these policies, contact people-ops@redwood.ai.
